coding_note: Every non-numeric cell backed by a verbatim quote with a locator in the coding sheet. not_stated is never inferred. One agent caught and discarded a fabricated abstract sentence from an LLM summarizer and recoded from raw HTML.

papers.label: LongMem
papers.f4_note: ICL tables only; headline ChapterBreak and perplexity claims carry no dispersion
flags: Headline ChapterBreak claim has NO stated N; F1/F2 both not_stated for it, F3 not computable.
F1 comes from a dataset-statistics table, not the abstract or a results caption; stricter reading gives not_stated.
F2 rule 2 is a coin-flip: PG-22 is one website (Project Gutenberg), ChapterBreak one (AO3). Read literally, F2=1-3 and F3>=500.

papers.label: MemoryBank
flags: All three quantitative arms are MemoryBank-equipped; the table contains no memory-free comparator, so its differences are attributable to base LLM, not to MemoryBank.
A memory-forgetting-ablation capability is claimed in the contributions but no such arm is reported anywhere; 'ablat' does not occur in the paper.
F2 could be 30 if the English and Chinese storages use disjoint user sets; the paper does not say.

papers.label: ChatDB
papers.claimed: 82% vs 22%, +60 percentage points; hard questions 28/35 vs 1/35
flags: NO metric definition exists anywhere in the paper. Whether grading is exact-match, human, or LLM-judged is never stated.
All F2 readings (rules 1, 2, and 3) yield a count of 1, so F3=50.0 regardless of rule choice.

The paper states an explicit extrapolation beyond its evidence: 'if ChatDB outperforms ChatGPT when the dataset is small, it indicates that ChatDB is also superior to memory-augmented ChatGPT when the dataset is large.' No such condition is run.

papers.label: Think-in-Memory
flags: Its GVD SiliconFriend baseline row is numerically identical to MemoryBank's own published table (0.809/0.438/0.680 and 0.840/0.418/0.428), suggesting the baseline was cited rather than re-run. The paper never states which.
Retrieval accuracy is undefined ('-') for the no-memory arm on KdConv/RMD, so that comparison has only one condition.

papers.label: MemLLM
papers.claimed: TARGET PPL improves by .524 (2.986 vs 3.510); editing AVG .84
papers.paired: paired by items but never stated as such; editing baselines copied from prior work
flags: F2 carried as a range per DL-58: 1 under the sequential-lifetime clause, 1000 if that clause covers only agent trajectories.
F1 sits on a secondary results table. The primary result is perplexity (Table 2), which reports no N at all.

papers.label: Zep (DMR arm)
papers.f4_note: IQR is reported for latency only, not for the headline accuracy
papers.paired: UNPAIRED against MemGPT (cited, not re-run); paired against the authors' own baseline at 94.4%
flags: The abstract's comparator is MemGPT's published number; the authors state they could not reproduce it.
Their own paired full-context baseline scores 94.4%, a 0.4-point difference, roughly 2 items in 500, about a fifth of the headline gap.

papers.label: Zep (LongMemEval arm)
papers.paired: no MemGPT comparison exists; authors could not get successful responses
flags: Carries the larger headline but the paper states no question count, deferring distribution details to the LongMemEval paper. F3 not computable.

papers.label: AgeMem
papers.claimed: 41.96% and 54.31% average; +4.82 and +8.57 points over best baselines
papers.paired: not_stated; no sentence asserts both conditions saw the same items
flags: Reports no evaluation-instance count in main text or any appendix; only training-side counts exist.
Its only non-answer text sits in the RL training reward ('optionally applying a penalty when no answer is produced'), not the evaluation metric.
